title: Language models trusted incorrect reassurances more than incorrect warnings in a defensive audit
summary: In tests of a prerecorded defensive audit dataset, incorrect reassurances moved language-model verdicts toward agreement more than incorrect warnings did. A prespecified check on seven additional model configurations found a mean asymmetry of 0.16, with a 95% interval of 0.10–0.24. This measures verdict behavior under controlled evaluation conditions.
ai_technology: DeepSeek; Qwen; GLM; Kimi audit models
organization: Seoul School of Integrated Sciences and Technologies; Liaoning Mechanical & Electrical College of Technology

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 Methods, experimental setup and §6.4 aggregate defensive behavior

evidence.tested: The study analyzed 16,572 evaluations on 916 matched pairs across eleven configurations. The seven-configuration confirmation used prerecorded samples and paired comparisons against valid evidence.
evidence.unknown: The confirmation was conducted by the same team. The data and decision conditions are controlled and do not measure real-world incidence.
evidence.ai_role: Eleven language model configurations independently evaluated prerecorded audit examples and supplied verdicts that were compared under paired evidence conditions.
